catalog.name: canvas-design
catalog.description: Design the HTML frames of a Canvas (mockups and prototypes of screens, pages and flows) so they look like one considered product, presented as a design document (foundations, components, then screens, each board with its states side by side), then create them with docs_write(canvas_create) or change a frame with canvas_update. Use when asked to design, mock up or redesign a screen, an app or a flow on a canvas, or to explore design directions.

catalog.name: drawio-diagrams
catalog.description: Draw and edit draw.io diagrams on the board (flowcharts, user flows, swimlanes, sequences, state machines, architecture, data models, plans) so they are clear, laid out on a grid, in one palette and safe to edit later, then look at the PNG and hand them in. Use when a structure or a process needs a picture, when asked for a diagram, or before changing an existing one; it also says when a Canvas or a Sketch is the better tool.

catalog.name: sketches
catalog.description: What an AI does with a Sketch (a person's freehand drawing on the board): read it, turn it into a diagram or a canvas frame, never draw one yourself, and put a screenshot on a Sketch only for a person to mark on. Use when a ticket or page shows a sketch, or when you think of drawing one.

catalog.name: docs-pages
catalog.description: Work in the board's Docs like a person does - write and edit pages (a spec, a decision, a how-to), link them with tickets both ways, format text the editor keeps (headings, tables, highlights, callouts, task lists, code, pictures and files), edit one part of a page safely without rewriting it, comment on a passage and answer a thread, turn a checklist into tickets, give a page to an AI member. Use before you create or change a Docs page, comment on one, or decide whether something belongs on a page, in a ticket comment or in a file of the repository.

catalog.name: working-a-ticket
catalog.description: REQUIRED for every AI member (the lead and each role) before any work on a ticket: how to work it from the first read to the report, and how to leave the ticket (status, criteria, closing comment) so a person sees what happened. Read the project first, plan, stay in your role, review your own work, report only what you did and saw.

catalog.name: working-with-tickets
catalog.description: How to use every part of a ticket on this board: a title, description and acceptance criteria a person can check, when to use a sub-task, a sub-ticket, a Story, a block or a link, how to keep the work log, a comment read in ten seconds, test cases and attachments as evidence, where files go (the worktree for code, the Workspace for outputs), and what each role writes. Use when you create, split, update, hand over or close a ticket, and when you make anything a person should see: a report, screenshots, logs, test cases and their proof.

catalog.name: evidence-and-handover
catalog.description: How to show your work and hand it over on this board: screenshots, test output and links as proof, a final answer or report the lead can act on, and a closing comment with what is left and the open questions. Use before you report, hand a ticket on, or tick a criterion.

catalog.name: repo-and-machine
catalog.description: How to work in the repository and on the machine without leaving a mess: branches, worktrees, commits and PRs, stopping the servers and watchers you started, ports, writing only inside your working folder, and where outputs for people go (the ticket's Workspace). Use before you change code, start a server or a watcher, write a file, or commit.

catalog.name: asking-and-writing
catalog.description: When to ask a person and how, when to decide yourself and say so, and how to write copy, comments and reports in the project's language (Vietnamese or English) so they read naturally. Use before you ask a question, choose between options for someone, or write text people will read.

catalog.name: working-together
catalog.description: How an AI team works on this board: the lead decides who does what, the roles are its subagents, and the ticket is the team's shared memory. Stay in your role, never redo another role's work, say plainly when you are blocked or disagree. Use at the start of every run on a ticket and whenever you need something from a teammate.

catalog.name: keeping-memory
catalog.description: How to keep the project's memory yourself, without being asked: what is worth remembering (a command that must be run a certain way, where something is, a trap, a person's correction or preference), where it goes (your role's notes, the ticket's notes, a lesson for everyone), and how to keep it short and true. Use whenever you learn something the next run would pay for again, and whenever a person corrects you.

catalog.name: docs-comment-threads
catalog.description: How to work the comment threads a person sent you from a Docs page: change the page, reply in each thread, and decide for each one whether to close it or leave it open. Use whenever a note says comment threads came from a Docs page (Send to AI), and whenever you answer a thread on a page.

catalog.name: brainstorming
catalog.description: How to work out with a person what to build before building it, and how to lay out options for yourself when nobody needs to be asked: questions in rounds, approaches with their trade-offs, an agreed list written down. Use when a ticket is vague or has several ways to go: a new feature, a Story to split, a scope to settle, a design direction, a solution to pick.

catalog.name: end-user-eyes
catalog.description: How to look at your work the way its real user will before you hand it in: the first-time test, the five-second test, jargon and translated-sounding words, walking one real task, and the machine-made look. Use before handing in anything a person will read or use: screen copy, an error message, a Docs page, a report, a slide, a screen.

catalog.name: office-files
catalog.description: How to make Excel, Word and PDF files that work and look considered, and how to look at any office file before handing it in: real formulas and styles, then rendering each sheet, page or slide to an image to check it, on whatever the machine has. Use whenever you create or change a .xlsx, .docx or .pdf file (decks: `slides`).

catalog.name: slides
catalog.description: How to make a presentation deck (.pptx) that looks designed and makes its point: the story first, a theme or the person's own template, pictures found or drawn, then every slide rendered and looked at. Scripts turn slides designed in HTML into an editable .pptx, fill a person's template, and render any office file. Use whenever you make or change slides, a deck or a presentation.

catalog.name: demo-video
catalog.description: Make a polished demo video (MP4, 1080p, as long as the story needs) of the Kanban board or any web app, with an intro banner, Vietnamese narration, captions that never cover the UI, camera zoom and spotlight, a hand cursor, click and typing sounds, lo-fi music and an outro card. Use when asked to record, make or update a demo, walkthrough, tour or showcase video of the app or of a feature.

catalog.name: role-triage
catalog.description: How Triage sorts a new ticket on this board: its kind, labels from the project's own set and the review depth, when to split, and what to do when the ticket is unclear. Use at the start of every Triage run.

catalog.name: role-pm
catalog.description: How the PM works on this board: planning a Story, splitting it into tickets each role can take, deciding when two roles disagree or a piece of work failed, and when to ask a person instead. Use at the start of every PM run: a Story to plan, a ticket to split, a question from a teammate, a ruling.

catalog.name: role-ba
catalog.description: How the BA works on this board: acceptance criteria a tester can check, the edge and error cases, and which document a piece of work needs (a feature spec, a bugfix spec, a decision table, a use case, an example map, a one-pager), with a template for each and a checklist before handing in. Use at the start of every BA run, and whenever you write criteria or a spec.

catalog.name: role-dev
catalog.description: How the Dev works on this board: reproduce first, a test that fails on an assertion before the fix, the smallest change, small commits on the ticket's branch, what to log, and the note for the reviewer. Use at the start of every Dev run and before you commit.

catalog.name: role-reviewer
catalog.description: How the Reviewer works on this board: what to look for in a change and in what order, what blocks and what is only a suggestion, and how to write a finding the author can act on. Use at the start of every review.

catalog.name: role-qa
catalog.description: How QA and QC work on this board: test cases written from the criteria (QA), every case run with its proof (QC), a failure reported so anyone can repeat it, and a criterion met only when its case passed. Use at the start of every QA run.

catalog.name: role-user-tester
catalog.description: How the User tester works on this board: become one real person, use only the running app in a fresh browser, walk the ticket's task the way they would, and report where they got stuck in their words, with a screenshot of every step. Use at the start of every User tester run.

catalog.name: role-tech-writer
catalog.description: How the Technical writer works on this board: documentation written for one reader and one task, every command and step tried before it is written down, the right kind of document, and where it belongs. Use at the start of every Technical writer run: a README, a guide, API or reference docs, release notes, help text.

catalog.name: role-devops
catalog.description: How DevOps works on this board: CI pipelines, builds, containers and environment config that are reproducible, pinned, least-privileged and proven to run, with secrets kept out of files and anything that deploys or spends money left to a person. Use at the start of every DevOps run.

catalog.name: role-security-reviewer
catalog.description: How the Security reviewer works on this board: follow untrusted input to where it is used, check a change for the common weaknesses, prove each finding with a safe local test, rate it by what an attacker gains, and report fixes without changing the code. Use at the start of every security review.

catalog.name: role-data-analyst
catalog.description: How the Data analyst works on this board: turn a question into exact definitions, look at the data before trusting it, compute in a script anyone can rerun, and answer first with the numbers, one honest chart and the caveats. Use at the start of every Data analyst run.
